Elements.description: Array of length n(n-1)/2, where n is equal to the number of components in SequencedComponentList, comprising the lower triangle of kij values within the binary interaction coefficient matrix in (row,column) order, e.g., [kij value for (2,1), kij value for (3,1), kij value for (3,2), kij value for (4,1), kij value for (4,2), kij value for (4,3), value for (5,1), etc.].  Note the array does not include the values of the diagonal, i.e. where the row and column component are the same.

NonDimensionalVolumeShift.description:
Non-dimensional volume shift parameters used in the Peneloux et. al. volume correction within the cubic equation of state. For its usage, the component's molar volume accounting for the peneloux volume shift is equal to the component's molar volume without the peneloux volume shift MINUS the NonDimensionalVolumeShift times the b parameter.
A typical non-dimenional volume shift for Methane is near 0.02 for SRK and -0.19 for PR (Peng Robinson). A typical non-dimensional volume shift for n-heptane is near 0.15 for SRK and 0.02 for PR.
NonDimensionalVolumeShift.title: Non-Dimensional Volume Shift

DimensionalVolumeShift.description: Dimensional volume shift parameters used in the Peneloux et. al. volume correction within the cubic equation of state. For its usage, the component's molar volume accounting for the peneloux volume shift is equal to the component's molar volume without the peneloux volume shift MINUS the DimensionalVolumeShift.
DimensionalVolumeShift.title: Dimensional Volume Shift

LiFactor.description: A multiplication factor to correct the critical temperature calculated by algorithms within some simulator applications. There is only one Li Factor identified for an equation of state within a compositional model.

C1.description:
First coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the mixture molecular weight is given by MWmix = c1 x (MWw ^ c2 - MWn ^ c2) + MWn. Values provided by the original publication for c1 and c2 are 0.291, and 1.0 respectively.

In Pedersen 1987, the mixture molecular weight is given by MWmix = c1 x (MWw ^ c2 - MWn ^ c2) + MWn. Values provided by the original publication for c1 and c2 are 1.304 x 10^-4, and 2.303 respectively.
C1.title: C1

C2.description:
Second coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the mixture molecular weight is given by MWmix = c1 x (MWw ^ c2 - MWn ^ c2) + MWn. Values provided by the original publication for c1 and c2 are 0.291, and 1.0 respectively.

In Pedersen 1987, the mixture molecular weight is given by MWmix = c1 x (MWw ^ c2 - MWn ^ c2) + MWn. Values provided by the original publication for c1 and c2 are 1.304 x 10^-4, and 2.303 respectively.
C2.title: C2

C3.description:
Third coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.747 x 10^-5, 4.265, and 0.8579 respectively.

In Pedersen 1987, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.378 x 10^-3, 1.847, and 0.5173 respectively.
C3.title: C3

C4.description:
Fourth coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.747 x 10^-5, 4.265, and 0.8579 respectively.

In Pedersen 1987, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.378 x 10^-3, 1.847, and 0.5173 respectively.
C4.title: C4

C5.description:
Fifth coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.747 x 10^-5, 4.265, and 0.8579 respectively.

In Pedersen 1987, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.378 x 10^-3, 1.847, and 0.5173 respectively.
C5.title: C5

C6.description:
Sixth coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the reference rotational coupling coefficient is found by α0 = 1 + c6*ρrm^c4. A typical default value of c6 is c3 x MWo^c5, or 8.377x 10^-4.

In Pedersen 1987, the reference rotational coupling coefficient is found by α0 = 1 + c6*ρrm^c4. A typical default value of c6 is c3 x MWo^c5, or 0.031.
C6.title: C6
